messages:
alex: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selection + batching tweak I'm seeing prefix cache hit-rate drop ~17% in canary. Latency p50 up ~14ms. Putting raw metrics here for quick triage.
maya: Yep saw it on the dashboard. p50/95 both moved, error rate still low but tail tokens spiked. Grafana: https://grafana/redwood/d/abc123/prefix-cache
alex: Snapshot from the runtime probe (10:12):
```
pool: prefix
total_keys: 1_450_321
hit_count_1h: 2_731_002
miss_count_1h: 3_184_210
hit_rate_1h: 46.3%  <-- baseline was ~63% on same window yesterday
eviction_ops: 18_432
fragmentation_pct: 27%
```
sam: I replayed a 30m trace locally. Frag ratio jumped vs baseline (11% -> 26%). Heap shows many small slabs with ~40% internal slack. kv key histogram skew flattened — fewer long-lived prefixes surviving warmup.
nton i: Did we change key normalization or append anything to the cache key in the kernel-selection path? I remember an earlier opt that concatenates model_variant for routing.
lee: I instrumented the batcher yesterday — the new greedy batcher reorders requests by seq_len then constructs the batch key including ephemeral batch_id in one codepath. That would explain unique keys for identical prefixes across batch runs.
alex: Repro steps to see the issue locally (small script):
```
# replay N requests from sample trace
cat sample_prefixes.json | jq -c '.[]' | xargs -n1 -P8 -I{} \
  curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/generate -d '{}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer x'
```
Run old vs new batcher and compare /admin/kv/stats
sam: I ran that. Results: replay -> hit_rate(old)=64.1%, hit_rate(new)=42.5%. I can push the full pprof and slab maps to S3. Also noticed eviction churn increased ~2.5x.
maya: Short-term mitigations: 1) decrease TTL for ephemeral prefixes from 5m -> 30s, 2) bump compaction frequency (run compaction every 60s), 3) temporarily revert kernel-selection flag to fallback path. That should buy time.
sam: Maintenance API to force compaction (works on canary):
```
POST /admin/kv/compact?pool=prefix&max_age=30s
# response 202 accepted
```
infra-bot: ALERT gpu-node-43: runtime-worker-71 OOM at 2026-03-17T21:14:02Z — process killed. Recent full-gpu-mem usage spike correlated with eviction churn.
toni: Given that, we should avoid full revert across prod. Plan: revert kernel-selection flag in canary only, deploy canonicalization shim that strips batch-scoped metadata from cache keys, and add a unit test that fuzzes batcher->key generation.
lee: I'll open the PR for the canonicalizer + test. Also adding a perf test that replays the 1h trace in CI with a small cache to assert hit_rate delta < 5% vs baseline.
alex: Agree. For canary rollout: revert flag (canary), deploy canonicalizer, enable shorter TTL/compaction, watch for 2h. If stable, proceed to limited region rollout. @lee @sam take ownership.
sam: FYI I ran a quick sim: 1h trace replay on 3 nodes -> median hit_rate delta = -21% with current new batcher, worst-case -33% when concurrency spikes. Uploading traces to s3://redwood-dev/prefix-cache/regressions/23050.
qa-bot: Friendly reminder — open a regression ticket linking the trace, pprof, and the canary dashboard. Tagging regression label and severity medium.
maya: Good. I'll create the rollout checklist and monitor dashboard. If we see OOM or >10% hit-rate regression after 30m, auto-roll back. :thumbsup:
alex: Thanks all — priority on the PR + canary revert. Keep short updates in this thread.
